title: On a parity result for the symmetric square of modular forms with congruent residual representations: the imprimitive signed $\lambda$-invariant congruence (Theorem 4.14)
author: Jishnu Ray
work: On a parity result for the symmetric square of modular forms with congruent residual representations
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4.14 (source0.tex lines 977-980, source label prop: lambda), the non-ordinary counterpart of the paper's parity theorem for two modular forms with isomorphic residual representations and a_p = 0. The retained complete proof (lines 981-985) is short but is a genuine research-level chain rather than a routine verification: it must first convert the vanishing of the mu-invariant of the primitive signed Selmer group into finite generation of the imprimitive one (the article's cotorsion lemma), then identify the P-torsion of that imprimitive group with the imprimitive signed Selmer group of the residual module A[P] through the retained isomorphism (19), then transfer finiteness across the two congruent residual representations using the article's Proposition 4.13, which itself rests on a congruence of Wach-module Iwasawa cohomologies and of the images of the signed Coleman maps, and finally identify the lambda-invariant with the F_p-dimension of that P-torsion using the article's theorem that the imprimitive signed Selmer group has no proper Lambda-submodule of finite index. Every step is Iwasawa theory of signed Selmer groups over the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, and the residual difficulty is transporting mu- and lambda-invariants across two congruent residual representations, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises, where such invariants are computed for one explicitly given module.
